accepted.direction: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
accepted.originalExpression: hit the right piano key with just enough force and pace
accepted.surroundingText: We say that somebody has a touch for doing some activity - an ability to hit the right piano key with just enough force and pace.
accepted.answerLogic: 원문의 'hit the right piano key with just enough force and pace'는 피아노 연주라는 구체적 행위를 통해 실천적 지식이 지닌 신체적 감각의 정밀함을 묘사합니다. 이를 '완벽한 신체적 직관으로 과제를 수행하는 것(perform the task with perfect physical intuition)'으로 추상화 및 패러프레이징하여, 본문이 강조하는 의식적 자각 없는 숙련 과정을 나타냅니다.

options.text: memorize the musical notes step by step
perform the task with perfect physical intuition
play an instrument without any prior practice
ignore the rules of technical knowledge completely
share musical experiences with fellow experts

wrongOptionExplanations.1: 악보를 단계별로 암기하는 것은 지문에서 대조되는 '이론적(technical) 지식'의 특징이므로 논리에 어긋납니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.3: 사전 연습 없이 악기를 연주한다는 것은 실천적 지식이 경험과 습관을 통해 축적된다는 본문의 내용과 정반대입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.4: 이론적 지식의 규칙을 완전히 무시한다는 내용은 본문에서 기술적 지식과 실천적 지식을 대조할 뿐, 배척하라고 주장하지는 않았으므로 과확장입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.5: 동료 전문가와 음악적 경험을 공유한다는 것은 본문 마지막의 '경험 공유'라는 소재를 차용했으나, 빈칸이 요구하는 신체적 감각(touch)에 대한 설명으로는 부적절합니다.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸이 포함된 문장은 실천적 지식(practical knowledge)이 무엇인지 구체적인 신체적 비유를 통해 설명하는 부분입니다. 지문의 첫 문장과 두 번째 문장에서는 실천적 지식이 가르치거나 배울 수 없고 오직 전달되며 획득된다고 강조합니다. 이어서 후반부에서 실천적 지식은 습관을 통해 기술의 범위를 넓혀 의식적 자각 없이도 과제를 수행하게 한다고 부연합니다. 따라서 누군가 활동을 수행하는 '감각(touch)'을 가졌다는 것은 곧 실천적 지식을 활용하여 완벽한 신체적 직관으로 작업을 수행하는 능력을 의미합니다. 정답은 ② 'perform the task with perfect physical intuition'입니다. 오답 ①은 이론적 지식의 특징(과협소), ③은 지문을 정면으로 반박(주제 반전), ④는 지나친 과확장, ⑤는 본문의 일부 소재에만 기대어 논리를 이탈한 매력적인 함정입니다.
keyPoints: technical knowledge와 practical knowledge의 대조적 속성 이해
habit과 experience를 통해 무의식적 수준으로 발현되는 실천적 지식 파악
bodily metaphors(touch, feel)의 문맥적 의미 추론
accepted.passageWithBlank: Technical, book knowledge consists of "formulated rules which are, or may be, deliberately learned." Practical knowledge, on the other hand, cannot be taught or learned but only transmitted and acquired. It exists only in practice. When we talk about practical knowledge, we tend to use bodily metaphors. We say that somebody has a touch for doing some activity - an ability to _____. We say that somebody has a feel for the game, an intuition for how events are going to unfold, an awareness of when you should plow ahead with a problem and when you should put it aside before coming back to it. When the expert is using her practical knowledge, she isn't thinking more; she is thinking less. She has built up a repertoire of skills through habit and has thereby extended the number of tasks she can perform without conscious awareness. This sort of knowledge is built up through experience, and it is passed along through shared experience.

accepted.direction: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
accepted.originalExpression: without the cream and jam
accepted.surroundingText: Chloe had already started to eat hers without the cream and jam; in fact,
accepted.answerLogic: 원문 'without the cream and jam'은 할머니가 크림과 잼을 바른 것과 대조적으로 아무것도 더하지 않았음을 의미하며, 이를 'before she added any extra toppings'로 재진술했습니다.

options.text: copying exactly what her grandmother did
before she added any extra toppings
taking a sip of her sweet tea first
offering the rest to her grandmother

wrongOptionExplanations.1: 할머니는 크림과 잼을 발랐지만 클로이는 그냥 먹었으므로 행동이 반대됩니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.3: 차를 마셨다는 단어는 앞에 등장하지만, 스콘을 먹을 때의 상황과는 무관한 소재 연상입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.4: 샌드위치는 스콘 이전에 먹은 것이므로 흐름에 맞지 않습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.5: 할머니에게 자신의 스콘을 주었다는 내용은 본문에 없습니다.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 클로이가 스콘을 할머니와 어떻게 다르게 먹었는지를 묘사합니다. 앞서 할머니는 크림과 잼을 스콘에 발라 먹고 있었고, 클로이는 스콘이라는 이름조차 모른 채 이미 입에 거의 다 넣은 상태였습니다. 즉 클로이는 할머니처럼 크림과 잼을 바르지 않고(without the cream and jam) 바로 먹기 시작했습니다. 따라서 본문의 구절을 패러프레이징하여 '아무런 추가 토핑을 얹기도 전에'라는 의미의 ②를 유추할 수 있습니다. ①은 극성 반전, ③과 ④는 앞서 나온 소재를 활용한 함정입니다.
keyPoints: 등장인물의 행동 변화 파악
순서 및 사건의 흐름 이해
특정 구절의 의미를 유지하면서 단어를 바꾸어 표현(Paraphrase)하는 능력
accepted.passageWithBlank: When the tea tray was being carried across the room to their table, Chloe's eyes rounded and she almost gasped out loud. There were lots of tiny desserts and mini sandwiches and small biscuit-looking things. Where to start? Where to start? Her grandmother smiled and winked at her from across the table. Chloe winked back. She took a sip of the sweet tea and waited for her grandmother to make the first move. She carefully mirrored her grandmother's actions and started with a small, delicate sandwich. It was good. She ate it up and selected another. After a time, all the sandwiches were eaten up and Chloe boldly chose the biscuit-looking thing before her grandmother. "Aren't the scones lovely, dear?" asked her grandmother, as she spread cream and jam on hers. Scones, was that what they were called? Chloe had already started to eat hers _____; in fact, it was mostly all in her mouth already.

accepted.direction: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
accepted.originalExpression: this is the exception rather than the norm
accepted.surroundingText: to make sure that in the long term, this is the exception rather than the norm.
accepted.answerLogic: 마지막 문장에서 필자는 장기적으로 단기적 긴급성 때문에 자기 돌봄을 희생하는 현상('this')이 '예외'가 되어야지 '일반적 규범(the norm)'이 되어서는 안 된다고 결론짓고 있음. 이를 '습관적인 관행이 되는 것을 방지하다(does not become a habitual practice)'라는 의미로 환언함.

options.text: such negligence does not become a habitual practice
postponing self-care fails to relieve immediate stress
personal well-being is temporarily suspended for short-term goals
personal time is not constantly disrupted by sudden deadlines

wrongOptionExplanations.2: 부정어(fails)를 포함한 오답으로, 스트레스 완화 여부는 본문의 핵심 논지(누적 효과 경계)와 무관합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.3: 단기적 목표를 위해 자기 돌봄을 유보하라는 것은 필자가 경계하는 상황이므로 글의 최종 결론과 정반대입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.4: 부정어(not)가 있어 매력적이지만, this가 지칭하는 바(자기 돌봄 포기)와 연결되지 않으며 본문의 단어(deadlines)를 이용한 소재 연상 함정입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.5: 자기 돌봄이 직업적 생산성을 완전히 넘어서야 한다는 것은 본문의 주장을 극단적으로 확대한 과확장 오답입니다.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 글의 결론부로, 자기 돌봄을 후순위로 미루는 현상의 장기적 방향을 제시합니다. 앞서 지문은 이메일이나 회의 등 예기치 않은 일정과 마감 기한 때문에 우리의 좋은 의도(자기 돌봄)가 포기되는 상황을 묘사했습니다. 단기적으로는 마감 기한을 놓치는 것이 취미 활동을 놓치는 것보다 영향이 크겠지만, 필자는 마지막 문장에서 자기 돌봄을 우선하지 않는 것의 '누적된 영향'을 인식해야 한다고 강조합니다. 따라서 장기적으로 자기 돌봄을 희생하는 일('this')은 '예외(exception)'가 되어야 하며 '일반적 일상(norm)'이 되어서는 안 됩니다. 이를 가장 잘 환언한 ① '그러한 방치가 습관적인 관행이 되지 않도록'이 정답입니다. 선지 ②, ④와 같이 부정 극성을 띤 오답들이 있으나, 논리적 연결성에서 탈락합니다.
keyPoints: 빈칸 문장의 문맥상 지시어(this)가 가리키는 바(자기 돌봄을 후순위로 미루는 것)를 파악한다.
글의 후반부에 나타난 필자의 어조(cumulative impact 경계)를 바탕으로 결론을 도출한다.
원문의 'exception rather than the norm'을 의미상 일치하는 선택지로 재구성한다.
accepted.passageWithBlank: There are few of us who don't at least want to make time for self-care activities such as exercise, hobbies, or relaxation. We start each day with the best of intentions but then get stuck by the flood of email messages or pulled into an unexpected meeting. As we struggle to reprioritize so we can get everything done before our deadlines, often our self-care activities are the first thing to be given up. No matter how much we plan, we all occasionally have days when that happens. In the short term, the impact of missing that grant deadline may be greater than the impact of missing a woodworking class. But it's important to recognize the cumulative impact of not prioritizing self-care and to make sure that in the long term, _____.

accepted.direction: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
accepted.originalExpression: no fixed conclusions about a so-called "national character" should be drawn
accepted.surroundingText: That is, no fixed conclusions about a so-called "national character" should be drawn.
accepted.answerLogic: 원문은 '소위 국민성에 대해 어떤 고정된 결론도 내려져서는 안 된다'이다. 패러프레이즈로 '특정 민족의 고유한 특성이라는 환상에 바탕을 둔 단정적인 판단을 삼가야 한다'는 취지로 재진술한다.

options.text: definite judgments based on the illusion of a unique national essence must be avoided
the historical origins of classical and Biblical proverbs must be clearly identified
we should reject the notion that any proverb reflects modern cultural values
proverbs determine the other social and cultural indicators within an entire civilization
the frequent usage of proverbs offers precise insights into a so-called national character

wrongOptionExplanations.2: 본문에 등장한 'classical, Biblical'이라는 소재를 차용했으나, 기원을 파악해야 한다는 것은 글의 초점과 거리가 멀다.
wrongOptionExplanations.3: 속담이 현대 문화적 가치와 전혀 무관하다는 'reject the notion'은 후반부에 속담이 문화적 지표로 쓰일 수 있다는 부분과 모순(과확장)된다.
wrongOptionExplanations.4: 본문의 'social and cultural indicators'를 빌렸으나, 속담이 다른 지표를 '결정한다'는 것은 본문에 없는 인과 왜곡(절반-진실)이다.
wrongOptionExplanations.5: 속담의 빈번한 사용이 국민성에 대한 정확한 통찰을 제공한다는 내용은 글의 전반부 경계(foolish to think of them as showing...)와 반대되는 극성 반전 오답이다.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 속담을 통해 한 민족의 정신을 해석할 때 주의해야 할 점을 제시하는 주제 역할을 합니다. 이어지는 문장에서 고전, 성경, 중세부터 내려오는 속담이 여러 문화권에 퍼져 있기 때문에 이를 상상 속의 국민성을 보여주는 것으로 생각하는 것은 어리석다고 지적하고, 후반부에서 특정 문화 내의 빈번한 사용 정도가 제한적 의미에서 지표가 될 수 있음을 강조합니다. 따라서 특정 민족만의 고정된 본성이라는 환상에 기대어 단정적인 결론을 내리지 말아야 한다는 ①이 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절합니다.
keyPoints: 빈칸 문장이 글 도입부에서 주제 의식을 드러내는 담화 역할을 파악하기
속담의 광범위한 공유와 특정 국민성에 대한 고정된 결론 사이의 관계(대조/제한) 이해하기
본문의 'imagined national character'와 'no fixed conclusions'를 종합하여 추상적 패러프레이즈로 도출하기
accepted.passageWithBlank: We must be careful when looking at proverbs as expressing aspects of a certain worldview or mentality of a people. That is, _____. There are so many popular proverbs from classical, Biblical, and medieval times current in various cultures that it would be foolish to think of them as showing some imagined national character. Nevertheless, the frequent use of certain proverbs in a particular culture could be used together with other social and cultural indicators to form some common concepts. Thus, if the Germans really do use the proverb, "Morgenstunde hat Gold im Munde" (The morning hour has gold in its mouth) with high frequency, then it does mirror at least to some degree the German attitude towards getting up early.

accepted.direction: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
accepted.originalExpression: hit their stride later in the day
accepted.surroundingText: but there are those who differ and hit their stride later in the day.
accepted.answerLogic: 원문 'hit their stride later in the day(하루 중 나중에 본래의 페이스를 찾다)'를 문맥상 'achieve maximum productivity rather late'의 의미인 'reach their peak performance in the evening'으로 패러프레이즈함.

options.text: adjust better to a strict morning routine
lose their focus and energy entirely
require more frequent breaks to recover
refuse to schedule any important tasks
reach their peak performance in the evening

wrongOptionExplanations.1: 아침 활동에 더 잘 적응한다는 것은 문장의 'differ'(대다수 아침형 인간과 다름) 논리와 정반대되는 극성 반전 오답입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.2: 오후에 집중력을 잃는다는 것은 본문의 생체 리듬에 따라 고점이 다르다는 논리와 맞지 않는 소재 연상 오답입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.3: 휴식(breaks)이라는 본문 어휘를 재활용했으나, 빈칸은 대다수와 달리 특정 시간대에 성과가 높다는 점을 나타내야 하므로 과협소 오답입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.4: 일정 조정에 대한 언급은 과도한 확장이므로, 오후에 높은 성과를 낸다는 본래 의미를 왜곡한 논리적 비약입니다.

regulate practices such as slaughter or experimentation, or may be more generally aimed at preventing cruelty. But
whether this kind of legislation is adequate lies at the heart of a key debate between those who argue, in a legal
context, for the promotion of animal welfare and those who argue for the promotion of animal rights. Those who argue
for animal welfare seek increased legal protection for animals from human-inflicted pain and other kinds of suffering
(for example, insufficient food and space). Animal rights advocates maintain that this welfare legislation does not go

accepted.passageWithBlank: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. It was an excellent device that would make it easy for shoppers to buy as much as they wanted without getting tired or seeking others' help. But Goldman discovered that in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not persuade his shoppers to use the wheeled carts. Men were reluctant because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping. Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. It was only a few elderly shoppers who used them. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop. A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was the turning point. A few shills disguised as regular shoppers easily _____. Within a few weeks shoppers readily accepted those carts.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸이 속한 문장은 실천적 지식(practical knowledge)이 신체적 메타포를 통해 구체적으로 구현되는 방식을 설명하는 예시 부분입니다. 지문 전반부에서 실천적 지식은 가르치거나 배울 수 없고 오직 실습을 통해서만 전달된다고 하였으며, 빈칸 직전에서 누군가가 어떤 활동을 하는 데 있어 'touch(접촉 감각, 솜씨)'가 있다는 것은 피아노 건반을 딱 알맞은 힘과 속도로 치는 능력이라 명시하고 있습니다. 따라서 이 능력을 학술적인 표현으로 패러프레이즈하여 '정밀한 강도(force)와 템포(pace)로 신체적 동작을 실행하는 것'으로 환언한 ③이 정답이 됩니다. ①, ②는 실천적 지식과 정반대되는 개념인 이론적·명시적 규칙에 치우쳐 있으며, ④와 ⑤는 지문의 논리적 흐름에서 벗어난 왜곡된 진술입니다.
keyPoints: 실천적 지식(practical knowledge)과 명시적 지식(technical, book knowledge)의 대조적 특성 이해

accepted.passageWithBlank: Technical, book knowledge consists of "formulated rules which are, or may be, deliberately learned." Practical knowledge, on the other hand, cannot be taught or learned but only transmitted and acquired. It exists only in practice. When we talk about practical knowledge, we tend to use bodily metaphors. We say that somebody has a touch for doing some activity - an ability to _____. We say that somebody has a feel for the game, an intuition for how events are going to unfold, an awareness of when you should plow ahead with a problem and when you should put it aside before coming back to it. When the expert is using her practical knowledge, she isn't thinking more; she is thinking less. She has built up a repertoire of skills through habit and has thereby extended the number of tasks she can perform without conscious awareness. This sort of knowledge is built up through experience, and it is passed along through shared experience.

question.surroundingText: The problem, therefore, is not one about treating animals inhumanely, but instead one about understanding them as human resources.
question.answerLogic: 원문의 'understanding them as human resources(동물을 인간의 자원으로 이해하는 것)'라는 표현을, 'viewing interactive living beings merely as instruments for human utility(상호작용하는 생명체를 단지 인간의 효용을 위한 도구로 바라보는 것)'라는 한 단계 더 높은 수준의 학술적 어휘와 추상적인 문장으로 패러프레이즈하였습니다. 본문의 'use by humans for food and as experimental subjects'와 'human resources'를 종합해야만 도출되는 종합적 재진술 논리입니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.④: 구제적인 법률의 실효성이나 집행력 약화를 언급하는 내용은 본문의 핵심 쟁점인 복지와 권리 간의 철학적 가치관 대립과 무관합니다.

question.explanation: 이 글은 동물 복지론과 동물 권리론의 관점 차이를 비교하며 동물 권리론의 핵심 주장을 논하는 글입니다. 마지막 문장은 '동물을 비인도적으로 대하는 것이 문제가 아니라, 동물을 인간의 자원으로 이해하는 것이 문제'라는 권리론자의 핵심적 비판으로 결론을 맺고 있습니다. 핵심 문장인 'but instead one about...' 이하에는 동물을 인간을 위한 수단이나 자원으로 바라보는 도구적 관점을 지적하는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 따라서 동물을 인간의 유용성을 위한 도구로만 취급하는 태도를 비판하는 ③이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다. 글의 흐름을 정확히 읽었다면 매력적인 오답에 빠지지 않고 정답을 고를 수 있는 문항입니다.

(③) 근거 — Welfare legislation accepts, they argue, that animals may be used by humans... the problem... is replacing them as human resources

question.passageWithBlank:
Many countries have had legislation to protect animals in place for decades, even for centuries. This legislation may
regulate practices such as slaughter or experimentation, or may be more generally aimed at preventing cruelty. But
whether this kind of legislation is adequate lies at the heart of a key debate between those who argue, in a legal
context, for the promotion of animal welfare and those who argue for the promotion of animal rights. Those who argue
for animal welfare seek increased legal protection for animals from human-inflicted pain and other kinds of suffering
(for example, insufficient food and space). Animal rights advocates maintain that this welfare legislation does not go
far enough. Welfare legislation accepts, they argue, that animals may be used by humans for food and as experimental
subjects; it merely tries to curb the worst excesses of these practices. The problem, on the rights view, is more
fundamental than this: animals are not the kinds of thing that humans should use in this way at all. The problem,
therefore, is not one about treating animals inhumanely, but instead one about _____.

_qualityWarnings.message: KILLER PARAPHRASE blank is too surface-level; use a richer central relation and a correct option with enough conceptual load.

accepted.passageWithBlank: Most people attack a new problem by relying heavily on the tools and skills that are most familiar to them. While this approach can work well for problems that are similar to those previously solved, it often fails, and fails miserably, when a new problem is particularly novel. In this circumstance, it is best to assume nothing and treat the problem as if you have never seen anything like it before. In martial arts, this sense of looking freshly at something is known as 'beginner's mind.' Beginners to any art don't know what is important and what is irrelevant, so they try to absorb every detail. Experienced martial artists use their experience as a filter to separate the essential from the irrelevant. When _____, then even seasoned masters can make mistakes.

accepted.answerLogic: 원문의 'feel like they are watching real people doing real things(마치 진짜 사람들이 진짜 행동을 하는 것을 보고 있는 것처럼 느끼다)'를 'witness authentic individuals rather than merely observing fictional portrayals(단지 허구적 묘사를 관찰하기보다는 실제의 인물들을 직접 목격하다)'로 품사와 어휘를 고교 2학년 수준으로 고급화하여 패러프레이징한 인과 귀결의 논리입니다. 정답 선지에 들어간 대조 접속사 'rather than'의 단서를 무력화하기 위해, 오답 ③번에도 'rather than'을 의도적으로 삽입하여 선지의 표층적 인상(Polarity)을 유사하게 일치시키고 깊은 독해를 통해서만 오답을 걸러낼 수 있도록 변별을 강화했습니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.④: 메소드 연기의 뛰어난 연기력 덕분에 관객이 감동을 느끼는 것을 넘어, 본인들이 직접 연기를 하고 싶어 한다는 추론은 주어진 글의 근거를 완전히 대상을 이탈하여 과장한 도약입니다.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 배우가 캐릭터와 완벽히 동화되는 메소드 연기를 펼쳤을 때 관객이 겪게 되는 최종 결과를 서술하는 결론의 역할을 합니다. 지문 중반부에서 배우들이 '가짜로 꾸며내는 것이 아니라 대본의 감정을 진심으로 느끼고(truly feeling the emotions... rather than faking them)', '캐릭터의 입장이 되어 본인의 편안함을 탈피한다(step out of their own comfort zone and into the character’s shoes)'고 명시하고 있습니다. 이러한 고도의 몰입이 가져온 결과(As a result)이므로, 관객 역시 영화 속의 단순한 가상 인물이 아니라 마치 실제 살아있는 사람들의 진짜 행동을 보는 듯한 경험을 하게 된다는 추론이 논리적입니다. 따라서 원문의 '실제 인물이 실제 행동을 하는 것처럼 느낀다'를 '단순한 가상 묘사를 보는 것을 넘어 살아있는 인물을 마주한다'로 수준 높게 재진술한 ②번이 가장 적절한 정답입니다. 정답 선지와 형태적 대조성을 맞춰 매력적인 유사 오답으로 구성했으나 내용상 흐름을 완전히 반전시킨 ③번이나, 본문 어휘 또는 지엽적 사실을 왜곡한 ①, ④, ⑤번은 정답이 될 수 없습니다.

accepted.passageWithBlank: Some actors completely immerse themselves in their roles by using a technique called method acting. Method actors seem to actually become the characters they play, and they may even continue playing the role after the cameras have been turned off. If necessary, they will change their sleeping patterns or their appearance, with the ultimate goal of truly feeling the emotions that are written in the script rather than faking them. Each role becomes a journey for the actor to explore a whole new identity. It can cause serious psychological and behavioral changes, sometimes even resulting in emotional trauma. In order to give the best performance possible, method actors step out of their own comfort zone and into the character’s shoes. As a result, audiences _____, not just fictional characters in a movie.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸이 포함된 문장은 앞서 언급된 'Over the Rainbow'의 옥타브 도약(스키마 위반)을 작곡가가 어떻게 해결하고 청중을 달래는지 설명하는 인과와 기제의 귀결 문장입니다. 본문의 앞부분에서 멜로디가 큰 도약을 할 때 우리의 뇌는 그것이 일시적일 뿐이며 결국 '출발점이나 화성적 고향(starting point, or harmonic home)'으로 돌아올 것을 기대한다고 언급했습니다(Gap fill 법칙). 따라서 스키마 위반인 큰 도약 이후에 작곡가가 청중에게 안도감을 주는 방식은 멜로디를 다시 안정적인 원래의 상태로 되돌려 놓는 것, 즉 ① '안정감을 회복하는 것(restoring a sense of stability)'이 됩니다. 이는 원문의 'bringing the melody back toward home again'을 자연스럽게 재진술한 것입니다.
keyPoints: Gap fill 법칙: 멜로디의 큰 도약 이후 원래의 출발점(starting point/home)으로 회귀하려는 음악적 기대감 이해하기

accepted.passageWithBlank: Melody is one of the primary ways that our expectations are controlled by composers. Music theorists have identified a principle called gap fill; in a sequence of tones, if a melody makes a large leap, either up or down, the next note should change direction. A typical melody includes a lot of stepwise motion, that is, adjacent tones in the scale. If the melody makes a big leap, theorists describe a tendency for the melody to "want" to return to the jumping-off point; this is another way to say that our brains expect that the leap was only temporary, and tones that follow need to bring us closer and closer to our starting point, or harmonic "home." In "Over the Rainbow," the melody begins with one of the largest leaps we've ever experienced in a lifetime of music listening: an octave. This is a strong schematic violation, and so the composer rewards and soothes us by _____, but not by too much because he wants to continue to build tension. The third note of this melody fills the gap.

question.passageWithBlank: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. It was an excellent device that would make it easy for shoppers to buy as much as they wanted without getting tired or seeking others' help. But Goldman discovered that in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not persuade his shoppers to use the wheeled carts. Men were reluctant because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping. Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. It was only a few elderly shoppers who used them. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop. A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was the turning point. A few shills disguised as regular shoppers _____. Within a few weeks shoppers readily accepted those carts.

question.passageWithBlank: Digital platforms have made a lot of work less sticky. As work becomes ever more modularised, commoditised and standardised, and as markets for digital work are created, ties between service work and particular places can be disconnected. While the business process of outsourcing that emerged in the 1990s allowed large companies to take advantage of a 'global reserve army' by moving their call centres to cheap and distant labour markets, cloudwork changes the volume and granularity at which geographically non-proximate work can take place. A small business in New York can hire a freelance transcriber in Nairobi one day and New Delhi the next. No offices or factories need to be built, no local regulations are observed, and ― in most cases ― no local taxes are paid. The switch in the production network of work happens by simply sending some emails or clicking some buttons on a digital work platform. And, in this way, the employer _____ in the places where it was once an employer.

accepted.explanation: 빈칸은 문화적으로 부응하는 교수법(Culturally Responsive Teaching)을 통해 비표준어 방언을 수용하며 표준어로 나아가도록 지도할 때 얻어지는 결과적 귀결을 완성하는 자리입니다. 첫 문장에서 표준어가 가져다주는 경제적 및 교육적 기회를 역설하고 있고, 이후 교사가 비표준어 방언을 일차적으로 수용하면서 이를 바탕으로 표준어 사용을 점진적으로 유도하는 대화 양상을 유기적으로 연결하고 있습니다. 즉각적인 결과는 보이지 않더라도 장기적인 성취와 학교에 대한 긍정적 태도 형성이 가치 있다는 논지에 부합하기 위해서는, 언어적 도약과 심리적 유대 모두를 지속적으로 이끌어낸다는 명제가 들어가야 합니다. 따라서 원문의 'the long-range benefits'를 추상적으로 포착하고 언어·태도 발달의 가치를 담아낸 ②가 정답입니다.
keyPoints: 비표준어 방언에 대한 바람직한 교수 역량과 점진적 표준어 전환 교육의 유효성 파악
양보절(~가 바로 나타나지는 않겠지만)과 주절의 양면적 대조 및 장기적 성과의 수렴 이해
구체적인 교사의 발화 예시(Oh, you don't have a pencil)에 담긴 점진적 보완의 철학 추론
accepted.passageWithBlank: Standard English allows access to certain educational and economic opportunities, which is the primary reason for teaching it. Students realize this when they interview for a first job or when they plan for post-high school education. So, what should teachers do when a student says, "I ain't got no pencil," or brings some other nonstandard dialect into the classroom? Opinions vary from 'rejection and correction' to complete acceptance. The approach most consistent with culturally responsive teaching is to first accept the dialect and then build on it. For example, when the student says, "I ain't got no pencil," the teacher might say, "Oh, you don't have a pencil. What should you do, then?" Although results won't be apparent immediately, _____ ― both for language development and attitudes toward school ― are worthwhile.

Many countries have had legislation to protect animals in place for decades, even for centuries. This legislation may
regulate practices such as slaughter or experimentation, or may be more generally aimed at preventing cruelty. But
whether this kind of legislation is adequate lies at the heart of a key debate between those who argue, in a legal
context, for the promotion of animal welfare and those who argue for the promotion of animal rights. Those who argue
for animal welfare seek increased legal protection for animals from human-inflicted pain and other kinds of suffering
(for example, insufficient food and space). Animal rights advocates maintain that this welfare legislation does not go
far enough. Welfare legislation accepts, they argue, that animals may be used by humans for food and as experimental
subjects; it merely tries to curb the worst excesses of these practices. The problem, on the rights view, is more
fundamental than this: animals are not the kinds of thing that humans should use in this way at all. The problem,
therefore, is not one about treating animals inhumanely, but instead one about _____.

question.passageWithBlank: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. It was an excellent device that would make it easy for shoppers to buy as much as they wanted without getting tired or seeking others' help. But Goldman discovered that in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not persuade his shoppers to use the wheeled carts. Men were reluctant because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping. Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. It was only a few elderly shoppers who used them. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop. A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was the turning point. A few shills disguised as regular shoppers easily accomplished _____. Within a few weeks shoppers readily accepted those carts.

accepted.passageWithBlank: Melody is one of the primary ways that our expectations are controlled by composers. Music theorists have identified a principle called gap fill; in a sequence of tones, if a melody makes a large leap, either up or down, the next note should change direction. A typical melody includes a lot of stepwise motion, that is, adjacent tones in the scale. If the melody makes a big leap, theorists describe a tendency for the melody to "want" to return to the jumping-off point; this is another way to say that our brains expect that the leap was only temporary, and tones that follow need to bring us closer and closer to our starting point, or harmonic "home." In "Over the Rainbow," the melody begins with one of the largest leaps we've ever experienced in a lifetime of music listening: an octave. This is a strong schematic violation, and so the composer rewards and soothes us by bringing the melody back toward home again, but not by too much because he wants to continue to build tension. The third note of this melody _____.

Baby Boomers most likely went to their local library, searched card catalogues, took longhand notes, and painstakingly typed their papers on a typewriter. Their challenge was in finding information. They memorized things like how to spell words, because reference materials weren’t readily available and the process of checking was time consuming. Memorization and precision are less essential as well — it’s easy to check facts and spelling. We’re all less patient and less able to focus, and we all want things faster. It’s no wonder we’ve replaced the word “trend” with “trending.” We barely alight on a new idea long enough for it to be a trend; it’s just zipping by or “trending.”

However, the necessity of present-ing music - making it present here and now, without __(C) which__ it will not be music at all - does not sit easily with a concept of education that rests mainly upon received factual knowledge and which, by tradition, uses the past to make sense of the present. If we want music __(D) to have__ a role in general education, it would seem logical to acknowledge this difference and give prominence to activities that will involve all pupils __(E) to work__ directly with music. Memorization and precision are less essential as well — it’s easy to check facts and spelling. This means that those brain activities don’t get the workout today that they did for previous generations of high school students. We’re all less patient and less able to focus, and we all want things faster. question.passageWithMarkers: Recent evidence suggests that the common ancestor of Neanderthals and modern people, __(A) living__ about 400,000 years ago, may have already been using pretty sophisticated language. If language is __(B) based__ on genes and is the key to cultural evolution, and Neanderthals had language, then why did the Neanderthal toolkit show so little cultural change? They have no idea who their real parents are or why they were put up for adoption, and all their attempts to discover this information __(A) are__ met with firm resistance from the government. In short, adoption officials will tell __(B) them__ nothing. However, in the past decade, many adoptees have publicly protested this situation, and some states have changed their previous policies. Those men and women who are __(C) desperate__ to find __(D) what__ they want to know will, if they can afford it, hire a detective to find out. markedExpressions.label: (A)

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This is what happens when life throws us a curveball.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주어 'we'가 향해진 상태를 나타내므로 수동태 'are headed'가 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사가 없고 뒤에 불완전한 절(주어가 없음)이 이어지므로 관계대명사 'what'은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 동사 'is'의 주격 보어 자리이므로 형용사 'unpredictable'이 적절히 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'end up ~ing' 구문으로 '~하게 되다'라는 뜻을 나타내므로 동명사 'spending'의 사용은 옳습니다.

accepted.explanation: 이 문항은 능수동의 구별 및 동명사의 목적어 취함 여부를 묻고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 (E)의 'kept'는 전치사 of 뒤에서 명사 역할을 하면서 뒤에 목적어 'us'를 취할 수 없으므로 비문입니다. 이는 우주가 우리를 깨어있게 유지하는 주체적이고 능동적인 의미이기 때문에, 뒤에 목적어(us)와 목적격 보어(awake)를 취할 수 있는 동명사형인 'keeping'으로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (E) 분사능수동 — 뒤에 이어지는 목적어 유무와 의미로 판정
(B) 관계사 — 선행사 없는 명사절을 이끄는 what
(A) 분사능수동 — 타동사의 수동형태 숙어 확인
accepted.passageWithMarkers: We know where we are __(A) headed__ and what we want to do. However, quite often, due to forces outside our control, things do not go as we had planned and we have to adjust to a postponement or create a whole new set of circumstances. This is __(B) what__ happens when life throws us a curveball. The fact is that life is __(C) unpredictable__. For example, your car breaks down and you are late for an appointment. While it is true that you never arrive at that important meeting, you end up __(D) spending__ a few relaxing hours with people you would never have met otherwise. Remember that not only are curveballs the universe's way of __(E) kept__ us awake ― which is a gift in and of itself ― but they are also its method of bringing us wonderful surprises.

claims.quote: 우주가 우리를 깨어있게 유지하는 주체적이고 능동적인 의미이기 때문에, 뒤에 목적어(us)와 목적격 보어(awake)를 취할 수 있는 동명사형인 'keeping'으로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
claims.evidence: 전치사 of의 목적어 자리에 오면서 뒤에 목적어 us와 목적격 보어 awake를 취하기 위해서는 동명사 keeping이 올바릅니다.

claims.quote: 주어 'we'가 향해진 상태를 나타내므로 수동태 'are headed'가 적절합니다.
claims.evidence: head는 특정 방향으로 향하다라는 의미로 be headed 형태로 자주 쓰여 상태를 나타냅니다.

claims.quote: 선행사가 없고 뒤에 불완전한 절(주어가 없음)이 이어지므로 관계대명사 'what'은 적절합니다.

markedExpressions.label: (E)

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 이탈리아 탐험가인 Christopher Columbus가 미국의 발견에 공로가 있는 것으로 '인정받는' 대상이므로, 수동태를 구성하는 과거분사 'credited'는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주절의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사 'honoring'으로, 뒤에 단수 정동사인 'does'가 뒤따르므로 어법상 올바른 동명사 주어 형태를 취하고 있습니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 선행사 'a new holiday'를 수식하면서 뒤이어 주어 없이 동사 'honors'가 오는 불완전한 절을 연결하므로 주격 관계대명사 'that'은 어법상 옳습니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'the diseases'이며, 그 뒤에 수식하는 관계절 'that Columbus and other Europeans brought with them'이 삽입되어 있습니다. 이 구조에서 문장 전체를 마무리 짓는 정동사가 와야 하므로, 준동사 형태인 'reducing'은 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 주어의 동작을 술어 동사로 서술하기 위해 시제와 어울리는 과거형 정동사인 'reduced'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (D) 정·준동사 — 수식어를 제외한 문장 전체의 본동사 자리 구별하기
(B) to-v/v-ing — 문장에서 주어 역할을 수행하는 동명사구의 형성
(C) 병렬구조 — 등위접속사로 연결되는 과거 시제 동사의 형태 일치
question.passageWithMarkers: Every year on the second Monday of October, the United States celebrates Columbus Day. This holiday honors Christopher Columbus, the Italian explorer who is __(A) credited__ with discovering America on October 12, 1492. However, considering his mistreatment of Native Americans and the devastating effect of his arrival, __(B) honoring__ the explorer does not make any sense at all. After arriving on the continent, Columbus killed and __(C) enslaved__ thousands of Native Americans. Additionally, the diseases that Columbus and other Europeans brought with them severely __(D) reducing__ the population of Native Americans. Therefore, the entire country should support the creation of a new holiday __(E) that__ honors Native Americans and remembers their suffering. As an alternative to Columbus Day, Americans should celebrate Native American Day or Indigenous Peoples’ Day.

accepted.passageWithMarkers: Inefficient teachers __(A) overlook__ the potential power of the opening minutes of class. Often, if students are quiet enough and if there are many pressing demands on a teacher's time at that moment, more than ten minutes can disappear before class starts. It's no wonder that students are late for class; they have little reason to be on time. You can use the first ten minutes __(B) to get__ your class off to a great start, or you can choose to waste this time. The first minutes set the tone for the rest of the class. __(C) If__ you are prepared for class and __(D) have taught__ your students an opening routine, they can use this brief time to make mental and emotional transitions from the last class or subject and prepare to focus on learning new material. In summary, you should establish an opening routine __(E) developed__ your class with an effective start.

accepted.passageWithMarkers: In the film The Karate Kid, the teenaged Daniel asks the wise Mr. Miyagi __(A) to teach__ him karate. The old man agrees and orders Daniel first to wax his car in precisely __(B) opposed__ circular motions. Then he tells Daniel to paint his wooden fence in precise up and down motions. Finally, he makes Daniel __(C) to hammer__ nails to repair a wall. Daniel is puzzled at first, then angry. He wants to learn the martial arts so he can defend himself. accepted.passageWithMarkers: Music has no past; it exists only at the moment when it happens, and no two performances are identical. This is music's greatest asset because it brings out the essential 'now' without implications of a past and a potential future. Thus, Stravinsky pointed out that only through music __(A) are__ we able to 'realize the present.' Musical 'meaning' cannot be __(B) separated__ from the act of presentation. However, the necessity of present-ing music - making it present here and now, without __(C) which__ it will not be music at all - does not sit easily with a concept of education that rests mainly upon received factual knowledge and which, by tradition, uses the past __(D) to make__ sense of the present. If we want music to have a role in general education, it would seem logical to acknowledge this difference and give prominence to activities that will involve all pupils working directly with music. Yet, in spite of numerous attempts to develop a more musical music curriculum for the majority of school pupils, the emphasis is still on pupils __(E) to absorb__ factual information about music.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주어 'they'가 덴마크에 의해 제한을 받는 수동의 대상이므로 과거분사 'controlled'를 사용한 수동태는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 바로 앞에 나온 복수 명사 'they'를 대신하여 뒤의 government를 수식하므로 복수 소유격 대명사 'their'는 어법상 적절합니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 동사 'question'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며 불확실한 사실을 나타내므로 접속사 'whether'는 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: (C) "distributing"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "is distributed"로 고쳐야 한다. 정답인 (C)가 포함된 문장은 'Most of the whale meat and blubber is distributed...'로, 원래 지문에서는 올바른 정동사 'is distributed'가 사용되었습니다. 하지만 이 문제는 (C) 자리에 준동사인 'distributing'을 제시하여 정동사 자리에 잘못 쓰인 것을 찾아내도록 설계되었습니다. 'Most of + 단수명사구(the whale meat and blubber)'는 단수 취급하므로, 문장의 본동사 역할을 하면서 수동의 의미를 나타내는 single 정동사인 'is distributed'로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.
keyPoints: (C) 정·준동사 — 주어 'Most of the whale meat and blubber' 뒤에 문장 전체의 정동사인 'is distributed'가 필요함
(A) 능수동태 — 주어 'they'와 동사의 관계가 수동이므로 과거분사 'controlled'가 적절함
(D) 형부구분 — 동사 'take place'를 수식하는 부사 'quickly'의 쓰임이 적절함
question.passageWithMarkers: The Faroe Islands are a group of islands in the North Atlantic. Although they are __(A) controlled__ by Denmark, they have __(B) their__ own government. The people of the islands traditionally hunt pilot whales. They have done this for centuries, so whale meat and blubber are important parts of the local diet. The government insists the killing of whales is not done for profit. Most of the whale meat and blubber __(C) distributing__ for free to the local community, although some is sold in supermarkets. Multiple hunts are held each year under the strict supervision of the local government. There is a law that says each killing must take place as __(D) quickly__ and efficiently as possible. The government claims that the average annual catch is only about 800 whales and that this is a small percentage of the overall pilot whale population. However, environmental groups still question __(E) whether__ this practice should be allowed to continue.

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: You may be surprised to learn how long the shortest war in recorded history lasted.

markedExpressions.label: (B)

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The British ordered Zanzibar’s new leader to step down, but he refused.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The attack lasted for just 38 minutes, but it killed hundreds of Zanzibaris, forcing the new leader to flee

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: forcing the new leader to flee and the country to immediately surrender.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 의문부사 'how'가 뒤의 부사 'long'을 수식하여 '얼마나 오랫동안'이라는 뜻의 의문사구를 이루고 있으며, 간접의문문 명사절 내에서 주어 뒤에 동사 'lasted'가 오는 어순으로 적절하게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 타동사 'choosing'의 목적어 역할을 하는 간접의문문 절 내에서 주격/목적격 보어로 쓰인 의문대명사 'who'로, 문맥상 어법에 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 5형식 동사 'order'는 목적격 보어로 to-부정사를 취하는 대표적인 동사이므로 'to step down'은 어법상 올바른 형태입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): forcing의 목적격 보어로 쓰인 'to flee'와 등위접속사 'and'를 통해 병렬 구조로 연결되어 명사구 'the country' 뒤에 이어진 'to-v' 형태이므로 어법상 아주 적절합니다.

accepted.explanation: 주절의 주어 'it'에 상응하는 정동사 'killed'가 이미 앞에 위치해 있고 문맥상 대등하게 병렬을 이루는 정동사를 추가하는 접속사가 없으므로, 쉼표 뒤에는 분사구문이 이어져야 합니다. 밑줄 친 forced는 과거분사 형태로서 뒤에 'the new leader'라는 명시적 목적어가 따르므로 능동의 관계를 나타내지 못해 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 이를 목적어를 취할 수 있는 능동 의미의 현재분사인 forcing으로 올바르게 고쳐야 합니다. (E)의 'to immediately surrender'는 'to flee'와 등위접속사 and로 연결되는 병렬 관계로서 완벽하게 복원되어 단일 정답이 굳어집니다.
keyPoints: (D) 분사능수동 — 목적어 유무와 분사구문의 능동형 판정
(E) 병렬 구조 — to-부정사 보어가 and로 대칭을 이룸
(C) 목적격보어 — order + 목적어 + to-v 구문 학습
accepted.passageWithMarkers: You may be surprised to learn __(A) how long__ the shortest war in recorded history lasted. It was called the Anglo-Zanzibar War, and it lasted only 38 minutes. Why the war took place and the reason behind its brief duration are fairly interesting. The war broke out in 1896, between the United Kingdom and a small African island nation called Zanzibar. Before that time, the United Kingdom had a great deal of influence over Zanzibar, even choosing __(B) who__ the nation’s leader would be. However, when the leader of Zanzibar died in 1896, he was replaced by his cousin without the approval of the United Kingdom. The British ordered Zanzibar’s new leader __(C) to step down__, but he refused. Rather than surrender, he gathered 3,000 soldiers and ordered them to protect his palace. Three British ships were sent in response. They soon began to attack the palace, quickly destroying the new leader’s army. The attack lasted for just 38 minutes, but it killed hundreds of Zanzibaris, __(D) forced__ the new leader to flee and the country __(E) to immediately surrender__.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'in which'는 앞의 선행사 'a way'를 수식하며 뒤에 완전한 절(children learn about the world~)이 오므로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 전치사 'for'의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사 형태인 'developing'은 어법상 올바릅니다.

accepted.explanation: 이 자리는 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 관계절 내의 동사 자리입니다. 선행사인 'skills and behaviors'가 복수 명사이므로, 관계절의 동사 역시 복수형으로 수일치시켜야 합니다. 따라서 선행사를 수식하는 동사로 단수형 is를 쓰는 것은 복수 주어와 일치하지 않는 비문입니다. 따라서 is를 are로 고쳐야 합니다. 단수 명사로 헷갈리지 않게 전체 선행사 구를 확인하는 것이 중요합니다.
keyPoints: (A) 수일치 판정 — 주격 관계대명사의 선행사와 동사의 수 일치
(B) 전치사 + 관계대명사 구조 이해
(E) 의문사 + to 부정사 명사구 역할
accepted.passageWithMarkers: Animals as well as humans engage in play activities. In animals, play has long been seen as a way of learning and practicing skills and behaviors that __(A) is__ necessary for future survival. In children, too, play has important functions during development. From its earliest beginnings in infancy, play is a way __(B) in which__ children learn about the world and their place in it. Children's play serves as a training ground for __(C) developing__ physical abilities - skills like walking, running, and jumping __(D) that__ are necessary for everyday living. Play also allows children to try out and learn social behaviors and to acquire values and personality traits that will be important in adulthood. For example, they learn __(E) how to compete__ and cooperate with others, how to lead and follow, how to make decisions, and so on.

accepted.explanation: 밑줄 친 대명사가 지칭하는 대상이 무엇인지 파악해야 합니다. 문맥상 사람과 상품이 건너서 이동하는 대상은 앞서 언급된 'the River Thames(템스강)'입니다. 템스강은 단수 명사이므로 복수 대명사 them이 아니라 단수 대명사 it을 사용해야 올바릅니다. 따라서 them을 it으로 고쳐야 합니다.

(A) 능동 vs 수동 — 분사구문의 의미상 주어와의 능동/수동 판정
(E) 전치사의 목적어 — 전치사 뒤에 오는 동명사 형태
accepted.passageWithMarkers: Marc Isambard Brunel (1769—1849) is best known for the design and construction of the Thames Tunnel. Originally __(A) born__ in France, Brunel escaped to the United States during the French Revolution. He later moved to London. When the Napoleonic Wars were at their height, he invented machines for __(B) making__ boots. During the Napoleonic Wars, Brunel’s factory supplied British troops with boots. After the Wars ended, however, the government stopped buying his boots and he went out of business. A few years later, Brunel was __(C) imprisoned__ for several months because of his debt. At that time, London was very much divided by the River Thames and needed more ways for people and goods to move across __(D) them__. In 1825, Brunel designed a tunnel under the river. The Thames Tunnel officially opened on 25 March 1843, and Brunel, despite __(E) being__ in ill health, attended the opening ceremony.

question.explanation: 주어로 쓰인 'Some of the ways'(관계사절 'we helped the CEOs remove their masks'의 수식을 받음)에서 핵심 주어는 복수 대명사 'Some'입니다. 따라서 문장 전체의 서술어 역할을 할 복수형 정동사가 필요한 자리입니다. 그러나 (D)의 'being'은 준동사(현재분사/동명사)이므로 문장을 완결할 수 없게 만들어 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 복수 주어 Some에 수일치되면서 과거 시제를 나타낼 수 있는 복수형 정동사 'were'로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 정동사/준동사 구별 — 수식받는 주어 뒤에 문장의 서술어 역할을 할 복수형 정동사 were 확인
(A) 동명사의 명사구 주어 — 주어 역할을 할 수 있는 명사적 성격의 동명사구 구조 파악
(C) 분사구문의 능수동 — 주절과의 동작 관계가 능동이므로 현재분사인 creating 확인
question.passageWithMarkers: Masks are too heavy to uphold indefinitely, and no matter how well you believe you are disguising yourself, others always know. The consequences are that you waste energy, sacrifice productivity, and lose people's trust. In our study, all of the CEOs were concerned that __(A) dropping__ their masks would make them appear weak. In every case, however, the leader's subordinates __(B) perceived__ the removal of the mask as an act of strength and courage. This, in turn, encouraged a culture where those subordinates did the same, __(C) creating__ a snowball effect. Some of the ways we helped the CEOs remove their masks __(D) being__ to actually name the masks, explore the significant personal and professional costs of upholding them, and ask the CEOs to reflect on the leader they most admired. At this point each of the CEOs was ready to rebuild a leadership identity __(E) based__ on values, strengths, and ambitions.

keyPoints: (D) 전치사의 목적어 — 전치사 뒤 명사·동명사 결합 판단
(E) 동명사 주어 — 명사 역할을 하는 준동사 자리 확인
(A) 과거분사 후치수식 — 관계 대명사와 be동사의 생략 및 수동 관계 파악
question.passageWithMarkers: Certain species are more crucial to the maintenance of their ecosystem than others. Such species, __(A) called__ keystone species, are vital in determining the nature and structure of the entire ecosystem. The fact __(B) that__ other species depend on or are greatly affected by the keystone species is __(C) revealed__ when the keystone species is removed. It is in this sense that we should draw attention to fig trees. Different species of fig trees may be keystone species in tropical rain forests. Although figs collectively produce a continuous crop of fruits, fruit-eating monkeys, birds, bats, and other vertebrates of the forest do not normally consume large quantities of figs in their diets. During the time of year when other fruits are less plentiful, however, fig trees become important in __(D) sustains__ fruit-eating vertebrates. Should the fig trees disappear, most of the fruit-eating vertebrates would be eliminated. __(E) Protecting__ fig trees in such tropical rainforest ecosystems is an important conservation goal because it increases the likelihood that monkeys, birds, bats, and other vertebrates will survive.

accepted.passageWithMarkers: Sweeping statements have been __(A) made__ about the effect of clothing on the behavior of a child. It has been said __(B) that__ a child who is better dressed is better behaved, and that a child who is dressed like a cowboy is louder than he is when dressed in ordinary clothes. Clothing, however, might have a temporary effect on the behavior of the child, but not a lasting effect. That is, we would predict that a child who was dressed in his best clothes and __(C) whose__ mother stressed that they were ‘best’ would be better behaved for a short period, but by the end of the hour the child would have __(D) forgetting__ his clothes and would be acting as he would in old clothes. Likewise, the child who is dressed in a cowboy outfit might be very noisy while __(E) playing__ cowboys for a brief time, but he might soon change to another activity and be no more noisy than usual.

question.passageWithMarkers: To demonstrate how our minds have adapted, consider a typical high school task: __(A) writing__ a research paper. Baby Boomers most likely went to their local library, searched card catalogues, took longhand notes, and painstakingly typed their papers on a typewriter. Their challenge was in finding information. They memorized things like __(B) how to spell__ words, because reference materials weren’t readily available and the process of checking was time consuming. And they were careful and precise when typing — correcting took time. Baby Boomer brains were trained to focus, pay attention to detail, be patient, and have mental strength. Haste meant waste. Fast-forward to today. The Baby Boomer challenge of finding information is less relevant — information is extremely accessible. Memorization and precision are less essential as well — it’s easy to check facts and spelling. This means that those brain activities don’t get the workout today that they __(C) were__ for previous generations of high school students. Today’s young brains __(D) are heavily focused__ on scanning and processing mountains of information. Their brains are trained for speed. But it’s not only the young who are increasingly addicted to speed. Their saturation in and early use of technology makes them highly tuned __(E) to require__ more stimulation and become more easily bored — but everyone’s brains are changing. We’re all less patient and less able to focus, and we all want things faster. It’s no wonder we’ve replaced the word “trend” with “trending.” We barely alight on a new idea long enough for it to be a trend; it’s just zipping by or “trending.”

accepted.passageWithMarkers: Recent evidence __(A) suggests__ that the common ancestor of Neanderthals and modern people, living about 400,000 years ago, may have already been using pretty sophisticated language. If language is based on genes and is the key to cultural evolution, and Neanderthals had language, then why did the Neanderthal toolkit __(B) show__ so little cultural change? Moreover, genes would __(C) undoubtedly__ have changed during the human revolution after 200,000 years ago, but more in response to new habits than as causes of them. At an earlier date, cooking selected mutations for smaller guts and mouths, rather than vice versa. At a later date, milk drinking selected for mutations for __(D) retaining__ lactose digestion into adulthood in people of western European and East African descent. The cultural horse comes before the genetic cart. The appeal to a genetic change __(E) driven__ evolution gets gene-culture co-evolution backwards: it is a top-down explanation for a bottom-up process.

question.passageWithMarkers: Inefficient teachers overlook the potential power of the opening minutes of class. Often, if students __(A) are__ quiet enough and if there are many __(B) pressed__ demands on a teacher's time at that moment, more than ten minutes can __(C) disappear__ before class starts. It's no wonder that students are late for class; they have little reason to be on time. You can use the first ten minutes __(D) to get__ your class off to a great start, or you can choose to waste this time. The first minutes set the tone for the rest of the class. If you are __(E) prepared__ for class and have taught your students an opening routine, they can use this brief time to make mental and emotional transitions from the last class or subject and prepare to focus on learning new material. In summary, you should establish an opening routine to develop your class with an effective start.

question.passageWithMarkers: Music has no past; it exists only at the moment when it happens, and no two performances __(A) are identical__. This is music's greatest asset because it brings out the essential 'now' without implications of a past and a potential future. Thus, Stravinsky pointed out that only through music are we able to 'realize the present.' Musical 'meaning' cannot be separated from the act of presentation. However, the necessity of present-ing music - making it present here and now, __(B) without which__ it will not be music at all - __(C) does__ not sit easily with a concept of education that rests mainly upon received factual knowledge and which, by tradition, uses the past to make sense of the present. If we want music to have a role in general education, it would seem logical to acknowledge this difference and __(D) giving__ prominence to activities that will involve all pupils working directly with music. Yet, in spite of numerous attempts to develop a more musical music curriculum for the majority of school pupils, the emphasis is still on pupils __(E) absorbing__ factual information about music.

accepted.passageWithMarkers: Animals as well as humans __(A) engage__ in play activities. In animals, play has long been __(B) seen__ as a way of learning and practicing skills and behaviors that are necessary for future survival. In children, too, play has important functions during development. From its earliest beginnings in infancy, play is a way __(C) which__ children learn about the world and their place in it. Children's play serves as a training ground for developing physical abilities - skills like walking, running, and __(D) jumping__ that are necessary for everyday living. It is in this sense that we should draw attention to fig trees. Different species of fig trees may be keystone species in tropical rain forests. Although figs collectively produce a continuous crop of fruits, fruit-eating monkeys, birds, bats, and other vertebrates of the forest do not normally consume large quantities of figs in their diets. During the time of year when other fruits are less plentiful, however, fig trees become important in __(D) sustaining__ fruit-eating vertebrates. __(E) Would__ the fig trees disappear, most of the fruit-eating vertebrates would be eliminated. question.passageWithMarkers: Sweeping statements have been made about the effect of clothing on the behavior of a child. It has been said that a child who is better dressed __(A) is better behaved__, and that a child who is dressed like a cowboy is louder than he is __(B) when dressed__ in ordinary clothes. Clothing, however, might have a temporary effect on the behavior of the child, but not a lasting effect. Likewise, the child who is dressed in a cowboy outfit might be very noisy while __(E) playing__ cowboys for a brief time, but he might soon change to another activity and be no more noisy than usual.

question.passageWithMarkers: Recent evidence suggests __(A) that__ the common ancestor of Neanderthals and modern people, __(B) living__ about 400,000 years ago, may have already been using pretty sophisticated language. At an earlier date, cooking selected mutations for smaller guts and mouths, rather than vice versa. At a later date, milk drinking selected for mutations for retaining lactose digestion into adulthood in people of western European and East African descent.
